title: Holiday Prep: Fast‑Track Cranberry Relish with a Mandoline
meta_description: Skip the can and make fresh, zesty relish. Learn how a Mandoline Slicer makes fast work of your holiday cranberry relish for perfect texture every time.
html:
Thanksgiving side dishes often compete for oven space, but the cranberry sauce doesn’t have to be part of that battle. If you are looking to upgrade your holiday table with minimal effort, making a holiday cranberry relish mandoline style is the game changer you need. This method ditches the heat, preserves the bright, tart pop of the fresh berries, and creates a texture that canned jelly simply cannot match.

Most people reach for a food processor for this task, but that often leads to a mushy, uniform pulp. To get a relish with distinct texture and elegance, you need precision cutting. That is where the right tool comes into play.

Why Raw Relish Wins Over Cooked Sauce

Before we get into the technique, let’s talk about why raw relish deserves a spot on your menu. Cooking cranberries breaks down the skins and releases the pectin, creating that gelatinous consistency we all know. While traditional, it can sometimes be one-note in terms of texture.

Raw cranberry relish, on the other hand, relies on the acidity of the berries mixing with sugar to macerate the fruit. This results in a condiment that is crunchy, tart, and sweet all at once. It cuts right through rich dishes like roast turkey, gravy, and mashed potatoes. Because there is no cooking involved, you also retain the bright, vitamin C-packed freshness of the fruit.

Why Use a Mandoline for Holiday Cranberry Relish?

The biggest complaint about homemade relish is the prep work. Hand-slicing cranberries is tedious and dangerous because they are small, round, and prone to rolling. Chopping them with a knife often crushes them before they even hit the bowl.

This is exactly why you should use a Mandoline Slicer. Restaurant-thin, even slices of veggies and fruit fast are the hallmark of this tool, and it applies perfectly to cranberries and their accompanying fruits. When you slice firm apples or pears paper-thin, they absorb the sugary cranberry juices much faster than thick chunks would. The Mandoline Slicer comes with adjustable mandolines with hand guards, ensuring you can process a bag of cranberries and a couple of apples in minutes without risking your fingertips.

Ingredients and Prep

For this recipe, simplicity is key. You want the tartness of the cranberries to shine, balanced by the sweetness of the sugar and the aromatic notes of citrus.

  • 12 ounces fresh cranberries, picked through and rinsed
  • 1 Granny Smith apple, skin on (for color and crunch)
  • 1 naval orange, thoroughly washed
  • 3/4 cup granulated sugar (adjust to taste depending on berry tartness)
  • 1/4 cup chopped pecans or walnuts (optional)
  • 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, grated or very thinly sliced

Step-by-Step: Making Holiday Cranberry Relish with a Mandoline

Start by setting up your workstation. You want a large cutting board and a bowl to catch the slices as they fall. Attach the hand guard to your Mandoline Slicer and set the blade to a thin setting—about 1/8th of an inch is usually perfect.

First, slice the apple. You do not need to peel it; the skin adds a nice ruby hue to the finished dish. Using the hand guard, run the apple over the blade. Because the Mandoline Slicer provides restaurant-thin, even slices of veggies and fruit fast, you will have the whole apple processed in seconds. Toss the slices into your serving bowl.

Next, slice the orange. You want to capture the zest and the juice. Slice the ends off the orange to create a flat surface, then cut it in half. Slice the halves into thin semi-circles. If you prefer a less bitter relish, you can trim away the outer pith, but leaving it on adds a classic marmalade flavor. Add these to the bowl with the apples.

Now for the cranberries. This is the trickiest part because they are small. If your mandoline has a safety guide or smaller teeth, use it. If not, you can use the hand guard to press down, but work carefully. The goal is to slice the berries in half or into thin rings. The adjustable mandolines with hand guards really earn their keep here, giving you stability while you slice these tiny, rolling fruits. Add the cranberries to the bowl.

Sprinkle the sugar and any optional add-ins like ginger or nuts over the fruit mix. Toss everything vigorously with a spoon until the sugar is dissolved and the fruit is well coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate. The relish needs at least an hour to rest, but letting it sit overnight is best. This allows the sugar to draw out the juices, creating a beautiful, syrupy consistency.

Serving Suggestions

This relish is incredibly versatile. Obviously, it pairs perfectly with roast turkey, but don't stop there. It is excellent on a leftover turkey sandwich the next day, adding a necessary acid kick to mayonnaise and bread.

You can also stir a spoonful into plain Greek yogurt for a quick breakfast, or use it as a topping for brie or camembert on a holiday cheese board. Because the Mandoline Slicer creates such delicate textures, this relish feels elegant enough for a formal dinner but robust enough for a casual family gathering.

FAQ

Can I use frozen cranberries?

Yes, you can. If using frozen cranberries, thaw them slightly and pat them dry before slicing. Frozen fruit can be a bit softer, so your slices might not be as crisp, but the flavor will remain excellent.

Is a mandoline really necessary for this?

While you can chop everything by hand, the texture will be chunkier and less consistent. A Mandoline Slicer ensures that the firmer ingredients like apples release their juices quickly, creating that signature saucy consistency without needing to cook the fruit.

How long will this relish keep in the fridge?

Because of the high sugar and acid content, this relish keeps very well. Stored in an airtight container, it will stay fresh in the refrigerator for up to 10 days, making it a great dish to prep ahead of the holiday rush.
